intro: From June 2024, Paper 3 mark schemes print a list that explains their signs. Paper 1 mark schemes use the same signs but do not print the list. Where the list explains a sign, the table uses its words. For the other signs, the meaning comes from how the mark schemes use them.

rows.meaning: The words on each side are alternatives. Any one of them earns the mark.

cites.quote: / separates alternative words / phrases within a marking point
Real time processing produces an extremely/fast response

rows.meaning: Two different answers that earn the same mark. Give either one.

cites.quote: // separates alternative answers within a marking point

rows.meaning: You do not need the words in brackets. They only show the context of the point.

cites.quote: ( ) the word / phrase in brackets is not required, but sets the context

rows.meaning: You must use this word, or a form of it such as a plural.

cites.quote: Underline actual word given must be used by candidate (grammatical variants accepted)

rows.meaning: The most marks that a group of points can earn.

cites.quote: max indicates the maximum number of marks that can be awarded
One mark per bullet point to a maximum of five marks

rows.meaning: Any of the listed points can earn marks, up to that number.

The first mark in a chain. The dashed lines under it are follow-on marks for adding detail to that point. The printed list does not explain it. Some mark schemes say a follow-on mark needs the first one.

cites.quote: First mark – any reasonable reason why a checker may miss issues when comparing two documents (1st)
(only award if either of previous two marks given)

rows.sign: only award if, NOT awardable if
rows.meaning: This mark depends on another mark. Without the first point, this one scores nothing.

cites.quote: NOT awardable if BP4 or BP5 not awarded

rows.meaning: Examples only. Other correct answers also get marks.

cites.quote: credit is given for valid answers which go beyond the scope of the syllabus and mark scheme

rows.meaning: This different wording also earns the mark.
This wording earns nothing, even though it looks close.

cites.quote: Sensor(s) are used to gather data (DO NOT ACCEPT ‘COLLECT’)

rows.meaning: The opposite statement counts on the other side, for example as a drawback instead of a benefit. It earns one mark only, not one on each side.

rows.sign: Max N marks if bullets/list of points
rows.meaning: A lower limit for answers written as a list. Mark schemes printed it from 2021 to 2024.

cites.quote: Max. six marks if bullets/list of points

rows.meaning: Name the type of software or hardware, not the product.

cites.quote: No marks are awarded for using brand names of software packages or hardware.
